2607.05477.title: Decision Protocols in Multi-Agent Large Language Model Conversations
2607.05477.paper_summary: Improving the task performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) is essential, yet scaling these models faces significant challenges such as diminishing returns and high costs. Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) offer a promising solution by distributing tasks among specialized agents to improve the overall task performance. This can reduce training costs at the expense of increased test time due to the discussion and decision-making process. The decision protocol is a critical component of MAS because it specifies how multiple agents collaborate to create a final solution. This thesis introduces the Multi-Agent LLM (MALLM) framework, which implements and evaluates various decision protocols, namely voting, consensus, and judge decision mechanisms, to simulate multi-agent discussions for conversational task solving. Unlike previous work that used a single decision protocol or tested them on limited datasets, this study systematically examines their impact on a diverse set of tasks, ranging from knowledge-based datasets (MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA) and logic-based datasets (StrategyQA, MuSR, Math-lvl-5, SQuAD 2.0). The results indicate that consensus protocols excel in knowledge-intensive domains while voting and judge protocols are more effective for logic-based tasks. Increasing response diversity through independent solution generation improves decision quality, while changes in information access during the decision process have minimal impact.
2607.05477.paper_summary_zh: 改善大型語言模型（LLMs）的任務表現至關重要，但擴展這些模型面臨著顯著挑戰，例如收益遞減和高成本。多代理系統（MAS）通過將任務分配給專門的代理來改善整體任務表現，提供了一個有前景的解決方案。這可以減少訓練成本，但由於討論和決策過程，測試時間會增加。決策協議是MAS的一個關鍵組成部分，因為它規定了多個代理如何協作以創建最終解決方案。本文介紹了多代理大型語言模型（MALLM）框架，該框架實施並評估了各種決策協議，即投票、共識和裁判決策機制，以模擬多代理討論以解決對話任務。與之前使用單一決策協議或在有限數據集上進行測試的研究不同，本研究系統地檢查了它們對多樣化任務的影響，這些任務範圍從基於知識的數據集（MMLU、MMLU-Pro、GPQA）到基於邏輯的數據集（StrategyQA、MuSR、Math-lvl-5、SQuAD 2.0）。結果表明，在知識密集領域，共識協議表現優異，而投票和裁判協議在基於邏輯的任務中更為有效。通過獨立解決方案生成來增加回應多樣性可提高決策質量，而在決策過程中信息訪問的變化對結果的影響則微乎其微。
2607.05477.author: Lars Benedikt Kaesberg et.al.
